prompt: Some volcanoes have a huge, broad crater many kilometres wide called a caldera. A caldera usually forms when:

options.text: A large magma chamber empties during an eruption and the ground above it collapses down into the space left behind
An explosion simply blows the top off the mountain in one piece
Rainwater dissolves the summit rock over millions of years
Glaciers carve out the summit during an ice age

explanation: Calderas are collapse features: when a magma chamber is partly emptied by a major eruption, the roof of rock above it is unsupported and sinks, leaving a broad depression much larger than an ordinary crater.
